title: Revenue Recognition ASC 606 - Complete Guide
learning_objectives: Master the five-step revenue recognition model under ASC 606
Identify and account for performance obligations in contracts
Calculate and allocate transaction price including variable consideration
Recognize revenue over time vs. at a point in time
Account for warranties, licensing arrangements, and consignment sales

common_question_types: Multiple choice on five-step model application

introduction.overview: ASC 606 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers) represents a comprehensive framework issued jointly by FASB and IASB to create a single, principles-based standard for revenue recognition across all industries. It replaced industry-specific guidance and established a five-step model to determine when and how much revenue to recognize. The standard became effective for public companies in 2018 and private companies in 2019.

key_principles.description: An entity recognizes revenue to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the entity expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services.
Revenue recognition is based on contracts with customers, which may be written, oral, or implied by customary business practices.
Revenue is recognized as performance obligations are satisfied, not necessarily when cash is received or when risks and rewards transfer.
Significant judgment is often required in identifying performance obligations, estimating variable consideration, and determining the timing of revenue recognition.

included: Contracts with customers to provide goods or services
Exchanges of nonfinancial assets (e.g., property, plant, equipment) not in the ordinary course of business
Collaborative arrangements when the counterparty is a customer
excluded: Nonmonetary exchanges between entities in the same line of business

five_step_model.overview: The five-step model provides a structured framework for recognizing revenue. Each step must be completed in order, and conclusions at each step affect subsequent steps.

step_1_identify_contract.title: Step 1: Identify the Contract with a Customer
step_1_identify_contract.description: A contract is an agreement between two or more parties that creates enforceable rights and obligations.

contract_criteria.explanation: The parties have approved the contract and are committed to perform their respective obligations
contract_criteria.cpa_tip: Can be written, oral, or implied; look for mutual commitment

contract_criteria.explanation: The entity can identify each party's rights regarding the goods or services to be transferred
contract_criteria.cpa_tip: Must be able to clearly specify what is being transferred to whom

contract_criteria.explanation: The entity can identify the payment terms for the goods or services to be transferred
contract_criteria.cpa_tip: Terms need not be fixed but must be identifiable

contract_criteria.explanation: The contract has commercial substance (i.e., risk, timing, or amount of future cash flows is expected to change)
contract_criteria.cpa_tip: Excludes sham transactions; look for economic reality

contract_criteria.explanation: It is probable that the entity will collect substantially all of the consideration to which it will be entitled
contract_criteria.cpa_tip: Assess customer's ability and intention to pay; 'probable' means likely (>50%)

contract_combinations.when_to_combine: Combine contracts entered into at or near the same time with the same customer if:
criteria: The contracts are negotiated as a package with a single commercial objective
The amount of consideration in one contract depends on the price or performance of the other
The goods or services are a single performance obligation
contract_combinations.example: A construction company signs two contracts with a customer on the same day - one for building design and one for construction. If the design fee is reduced because the construction contract was also awarded, these should be combined.

contract_modifications.definition: A change in the scope or price (or both) of a contract that is approved by the parties

accounting_approaches.when: Modification adds distinct goods/services at standalone selling price
accounting_approaches.treatment: Account for as a new, separate contract

accounting_approaches.when: Remaining goods/services are distinct from those transferred before modification
accounting_approaches.treatment: Terminate old contract and create new contract for remaining performance obligations
Adjust revenue as if modification was part of original contract; recognize catch-up adjustment

accounting_approaches.when: Mix of distinct and non-distinct goods/services
accounting_approaches.treatment: Apply prospective approach to distinct items and cumulative catch-up to non-distinct items

step_2_identify_performance_obligations.title: Step 2: Identify the Performance Obligations in the Contract
step_2_identify_performance_obligations.description: A performance obligation is a promise to transfer a good or service (or a bundle of goods or services) that is distinct.

distinct_criteria.overview: A good or service is distinct if BOTH of the following criteria are met:

criterion_1.title: Capable of being distinct
criterion_1.description: The customer can benefit from the good or service either on its own or together with other resources readily available to the customer
criterion_1.test: Can the customer use, consume, or sell the item for economic benefit without the other promised goods/services in the contract?
criterion_1.example: A software license is capable of being distinct if the customer can use the software independently, even if the vendor also provides installation services.

criterion_2.title: Distinct within the context of the contract
criterion_2.description: The promise to transfer the good or service is separately identifiable from other promises in the contract
criterion_2.test: Is the good/service highly interdependent or interrelated with other goods/services in the contract?
indicators: The entity provides a significant service of integrating the goods/services (outputs a combined item)
The goods/services significantly modify or customize each other
The goods/services are highly interdependent or interrelated (can't fulfill one without the other)
criterion_2.example: In a contract to design and build a custom manufacturing facility, design and construction are NOT distinct within context because they are highly integrated to deliver one combined output.

common_scenarios.analysis: Typically TWO performance obligations if installation is routine/simple; ONE if installation is complex/customized
common_scenarios.cpa_exam_tip: Look for whether installation significantly customizes or modifies the good

common_scenarios.analysis: Standard assurance warranty = NOT a performance obligation (accrue under ASC 460). Service-type warranty = separate performance obligation
common_scenarios.cpa_exam_tip: If customer can purchase warranty separately, it's service-type

common_scenarios.analysis: Each distinct deliverable is a separate performance obligation if both criteria met
common_scenarios.cpa_exam_tip: Evaluate both capability and context criteria

common_scenarios.analysis: Can treat as ONE performance obligation if: (1) each is distinct, and (2) same pattern of transfer
common_scenarios.cpa_exam_tip: Common for service contracts (e.g., monthly cleaning services)

immaterial_promises.principle: Entities may use judgment to assess whether promised goods/services are immaterial in the context of the contract
immaterial_promises.example: Free shipping on a product sale is often considered immaterial and not a separate performance obligation
immaterial_promises.cpa_tip: Focus materiality assessment on the contract level, not the entity level

step_3_determine_transaction_price.title: Step 3: Determine the Transaction Price
step_3_determine_transaction_price.description: The transaction price is the amount of consideration to which an entity expects to be entitled in exchange for transferring promised goods or services to a customer.

components.description: Stated contract price that does not vary
components.accounting: Include in transaction price at contract inception

components.description: Consideration that can vary due to discounts, rebates, refunds, credits, price concessions, incentives, performance bonuses, penalties, contingencies
components.accounting: Estimate using expected value or most likely amount method
components.constraint: Include only to the extent it is probable that a significant reversal will NOT occur

components.description: Time value of money when payment timing differs significantly from transfer timing
components.accounting: Adjust transaction price for time value; recognize interest income/expense
components.practical_expedient: No adjustment if payment < 1 year from transfer

components.description: Goods, services, or other noncash items received as payment
components.accounting: Measure at fair value; if not estimable, use standalone selling price of goods/services transferred

components.description: Amounts paid or payable to customer (or to parties that purchase from customer)
components.accounting: Reduce transaction price unless payment is for distinct good/service from customer

estimation_methods.description: Sum of probability-weighted amounts in a range of possible outcomes
estimation_methods.when_to_use: Large number of contracts with similar characteristics
estimation_methods.example: Software company offers volume rebates; expected value based on historical rebate patterns across thousands of customers

estimation_methods.description: Single most likely amount in a range of possible outcomes
estimation_methods.when_to_use: Contract has only two possible outcomes or one outcome is far more likely
estimation_methods.example: Construction contract with $50M base price and $5M completion bonus. If 90% likely to earn bonus, most likely amount is $55M

constraint_on_variable_consideration.principle: Include variable consideration in transaction price only to the extent it is PROBABLE that a significant reversal will NOT occur when the uncertainty is resolved
constraint_on_variable_consideration.threshold: Probable = likely to occur (generally interpreted as >75% probability)
factors_increasing_reversal_risk: Amount is highly susceptible to factors outside entity's influence (e.g., market volatility, third-party actions)
Uncertainty not expected to be resolved for a long period of time
Entity's experience with similar contracts is limited or not predictive
Contract has a large number and broad range of possible consideration amounts
Entity has practice of offering price concessions or changing payment terms
constraint_on_variable_consideration.reassessment: Re-evaluate constraint at end of each reporting period; update transaction price as needed

common_variable_consideration_types.example: Customer receives 5% rebate if purchases exceed $1M in a year
common_variable_consideration_types.approach: Estimate total purchases, determine if threshold will be met, apply constraint

common_variable_consideration_types.example: Earn $500K bonus for completing project 30 days early
common_variable_consideration_types.approach: Assess probability of meeting target, apply most likely amount or expected value

common_variable_consideration_types.example: $10K per day penalty for late delivery
common_variable_consideration_types.approach: Estimate likelihood and extent of delays, reduce transaction price

common_variable_consideration_types.example: History of accepting less than stated price to maintain customer relationships
common_variable_consideration_types.approach: Consider past practices and current customer circumstances

common_variable_consideration_types.example: Customers can return products within 30 days
common_variable_consideration_types.approach: Estimate returns based on historical data, recognize refund liability and asset for right to recover

significant_financing_component.principle: Adjust transaction price for time value of money when timing of payments provides customer or entity with significant financing benefit
indicators_of_significance: Difference between promised consideration and cash selling price
Combined effect of: (1) expected length of time between transfer and payment, and (2) prevailing interest rates in relevant market
when_not_required: Customer paid in advance and transfer timing is at customer's discretion
Substantial amount of consideration is variable and amount/timing varies based on occurrence of future event not substantially within control of customer or entity
Difference between promised consideration and cash price relates to reasons other than financing (e.g., protect from credit risk)
significant_financing_component.practical_expedient: Entity need not adjust for financing if period between transfer and payment is one year or less

calculation.step_1: Determine the discount rate (rate that would be reflected in a separate financing transaction between entity and customer at contract inception)
calculation.step_2: Calculate present value of promised consideration using discount rate
calculation.step_3: Difference between nominal amount and PV is financing component
calculation.step_4: Amortize financing component over payment period using effective interest method

example.scenario: Entity sells equipment for $121,000 payable in two years. Cash price is $100,000. Discount rate is 10%.
calculation: Financing component = $21,000 (recognized as interest income over 2 years)

journal_entries.entry: DR Accounts Receivable $121,000 | CR Revenue $100,000 | CR Contract Liability - Financing $21,000
DR Contract Liability - Financing $10,000 | CR Interest Income $10,000
DR Contract Liability - Financing $11,000 | CR Interest Income $11,000
DR Cash $121,000 | CR Accounts Receivable $121,000

types: Credits or coupons that can be applied against amounts owed

accounting_treatment.scenario: Payment for distinct good/service from customer
accounting_treatment.treatment: Account for purchase separately; if payment exceeds FV of good/service, excess reduces transaction price
accounting_treatment.example: Manufacturer pays retailer $50K for shelf space worth $50K = purchase of service, no reduction to revenue
Manufacturer pays retailer $50K slotting fee for shelf space but receives nothing distinct = reduce revenue by $50K

consideration_payable_to_customer.timing: Reduce revenue when the later of: (a) entity recognizes revenue for transfer of goods/services, or (b) entity pays or promises to pay consideration
consideration_payable_to_customer.cpa_exam_tip: Slotting fees, co-op advertising payments, and customer incentives are usually contra-revenue unless entity receives distinct good/service

step_4_allocate_transaction_price.title: Step 4: Allocate the Transaction Price to Performance Obligations
step_4_allocate_transaction_price.description: Allocate transaction price to each performance obligation based on relative standalone selling prices. The objective is to depict the amount of consideration to which the entity expects to be entitled for each promised good or service.

allocation_basis.general_rule: Allocate based on relative standalone selling prices (SSP)
allocation_basis.formula: Allocation to PO = (SSP of PO / Total SSP of all POs) × Transaction Price

standalone_selling_price.definition: The price at which an entity would sell a promised good or service separately to a customer
standalone_selling_price.best_evidence: Observable price when entity sells good/service separately in similar circumstances to similar customers

estimation_methods_when_not_observable.description: Evaluate the market in which goods/services are sold and estimate price customers would be willing to pay
estimation_methods_when_not_observable.example: Research competitor pricing for similar services

estimation_methods_when_not_observable.description: Forecast expected costs of satisfying performance obligation and add appropriate margin
estimation_methods_when_not_observable.example: Calculate cost to deliver service ($80K) plus typical margin (25%) = SSP of $100K

estimation_methods_when_not_observable.description: Total transaction price less sum of observable SSPs of other goods/services
estimation_methods_when_not_observable.when_allowed: ONLY when: (a) entity sells same good/service to different customers for wide range of prices (highly variable), OR (b) entity has not yet established price and good/service has not been sold separately
estimation_methods_when_not_observable.example: Software bundle: Total price $150K, Module A SSP $100K (observable), Module B SSP unknown and highly variable. Module B SSP = $150K - $100K = $50K

allocation_examples.scenario: Variable consideration allocated to specific performance obligation
facts: Contract for two distinct services: Consulting ($100K SSP) and Training ($50K SSP)
Variable fee: Up to $30K based on training session attendance
Variable fee relates specifically to training quality
allocation: Step 1: Determine if variable consideration relates entirely to specific PO
Step 2: Allocate $120K fixed fee: Consulting $80K, Training $40K (relative SSP)
Step 3: Allocate variable $30K entirely to Training PO (where it was earned)
criteria_for_specific_allocation: Variable payment relates specifically to entity's efforts to satisfy the specific PO (or transfer distinct good/service)
Allocating variable amount entirely to the PO is consistent with allocation objective when considering all POs in contract

allocation_of_discount.default: Allocate proportionately to all performance obligations
allocation_of_discount.exception: Allocate entirely to one or more (but not all) POs if:
exception_criteria: Entity regularly sells each distinct good/service in contract on standalone basis
Entity also regularly sells a subset of those goods/services at a discount
The discount is substantially the same as the discount in the contract

example.scenario: Entity regularly sells Products A, B, C separately for $40, $55, $45. Entity also regularly sells A+B together for $80 (15% discount). Current contract sells A+B+C for $125.
analysis: Entity regularly discounts A+B by 15% (from $95 to ~$80)
Therefore, allocate entire $15 discount to A+B; allocate full $45 to C

allocation_of_variable_consideration.general_rule: Allocate variable consideration using same SSP allocation method
allocation_of_variable_consideration.exception: Allocate entirely to one or more specific performance obligations if ALL criteria met:
exception_criteria: Variable payment terms relate specifically to entity's efforts to satisfy the PO (or to specific outcome from satisfying the PO)
Allocating variable amount entirely to PO is consistent with allocation objective given all POs and payment terms in contract
allocation_of_variable_consideration.example: License of IP plus consulting services. Royalty based on sales of IP-based products relates specifically to license PO, not consulting PO.

changes_in_transaction_price.general_principle: Allocate subsequent changes in transaction price on same basis as at contract inception
changes_in_transaction_price.variable_consideration_updates: When estimate of variable consideration changes, allocate change to POs using original allocation percentages (unless it relates specifically to one PO)
changes_in_transaction_price.example: If performance bonus estimate increases from $100K to $150K, allocate incremental $50K to all POs based on original relative SSP percentages

step_5_recognize_revenue.title: Step 5: Recognize Revenue When (or As) Performance Obligations Are Satisfied
step_5_recognize_revenue.description: An entity recognizes revenue when (or as) it satisfies a performance obligation by transferring a promised good or service to a customer. Transfer occurs when customer obtains control.

control_concept.definition: The ability to direct the use of, and obtain substantially all of the remaining benefits from, the asset
benefits_include: Using asset to produce goods or provide services
Using asset to enhance value of other assets
Using asset to settle liabilities or reduce expenses
Pledging asset to secure a loan
indicators_of_control_transfer: Entity has present right to payment for the asset
Customer has legal title to the asset
Entity has transferred physical possession of the asset
Customer has significant risks and rewards of ownership
control_concept.control_vs_risks_and_rewards: ASC 606 focuses on control, which may transfer at different time than risks and rewards. However, transfer of significant risks and rewards is an indicator of control transfer.

over_time.when: Performance obligation is satisfied over time if ANY of these criteria met:

criteria.criterion: Customer simultaneously receives and consumes benefits as entity performs
examples: Routine or recurring services (cleaning, security, payroll processing)
criteria.test: If entity stopped performing, would another entity need to substantially re-perform completed work? If no, criterion is met.
criteria.cpa_tip: Most common criterion for service contracts

criteria.criterion: Entity's performance creates or enhances an asset that customer controls as it is created/enhanced
examples: Consulting to improve customer's internal processes
criteria.test: Does customer control the work-in-process asset?
criteria.cpa_tip: Look for customer control of work-in-process

criteria.criterion: Entity's performance does not create an asset with alternative use to entity AND entity has enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date
examples: Construction of unique asset per customer specifications
criteria.alternative_use_test: Can entity practically direct the asset to another customer without significant economic loss due to contractual restrictions or practical limitations?
criteria.right_to_payment_test: Is entity entitled to payment that compensates for performance completed to date (including reasonable profit margin)?
criteria.cpa_tip: Both conditions must be met: no alternative use AND enforceable right to payment

measurement_methods.description: Recognize revenue based on value transferred to customer relative to remaining goods/services promised
examples: Surveys of performance completed to date
measurement_methods.advantages: Direct measurement of value transferred to customer
measurement_methods.disadvantages: May not be observable or may require significant estimates
measurement_methods.when_to_use: When entity's performance creates direct value to customer that can be measured

measurement_methods.description: Recognize revenue based on entity's efforts or inputs toward satisfaction of PO relative to total expected inputs
measurement_methods.advantages: Often readily available from entity's systems
measurement_methods.disadvantages: May not directly measure progress if inputs don't relate proportionately to progress
measurement_methods.when_to_use: When entity's efforts or inputs are expended evenly throughout performance period
measurement_methods.adjustment_required: Exclude costs that don't depict transfer of control (e.g., uninstalled materials, wasted materials)

cost_to_cost_method.description: Common input method using ratio of costs incurred to total expected costs
cost_to_cost_method.formula: Revenue recognized = (Costs incurred to date / Total estimated costs) × Transaction price allocated to PO
adjustments: Exclude costs that don't contribute to progress (uninstalled materials, wasted materials, defective products)
Update total estimated costs each period; recognize cumulative catch-up adjustment

point_in_time.when: Performance obligation does NOT meet any over-time criteria
point_in_time.description: Recognize revenue at point when customer obtains control

primary_indicators: Entity has present right to payment
Customer has significant risks and rewards of ownership
considerations: Evaluate when indicators occur (may be different points)
Use judgment based on specific facts

common_point_in_time_scenarios.typical_recognition_point: When customer pays and takes possession
common_point_in_time_scenarios.control_transfer_evidence: Physical possession, payment received, risks/rewards transferred

common_point_in_time_scenarios.typical_recognition_point: When goods set aside, customer has title, payment due, substantive reason for arrangement exists
common_point_in_time_scenarios.control_transfer_evidence: Legal title, right to payment despite no physical transfer
additional_criteria: Reason for bill-and-hold must be substantive (at customer's request)
Product must be separately identified as belonging to customer
Product must be ready for transfer to customer
Entity cannot use product or direct it to another customer

common_point_in_time_scenarios.typical_recognition_point: When dealer sells to end customer (NOT when inventory transferred to dealer)
common_point_in_time_scenarios.control_transfer_evidence: Entity retains control until dealer makes sale
indicators_of_consignment: Product controlled by entity until specified event occurs
Entity can require return of product or transfer to another party
Dealer has no unconditional obligation to pay

common_point_in_time_scenarios.typical_recognition_point: At time of sale, but recognize refund liability for expected returns
accounting: Recognize revenue for products not expected to be returned
Recognize refund liability for expected returns (reduce revenue)
Recognize asset for right to recover products from customer (inventory)

common_point_in_time_scenarios.typical_recognition_point: When goods shipped from seller's location
When goods arrive at customer location

costs_to_obtain_contract.definition: Incremental costs that entity would not have incurred if contract had not been obtained
examples: Success fees paid to third parties
costs_to_obtain_contract.accounting: Capitalize and amortize over period of benefit
costs_to_obtain_contract.practical_expedient: Expense as incurred if amortization period would be one year or less
not_capitalizable: Costs incurred regardless of whether contract obtained (e.g., bid and proposal costs, travel costs)

criteria: Costs relate directly to a contract (or specific anticipated contract)
Costs generate or enhance resources that will be used to satisfy performance obligations in future
Costs are expected to be recovered
examples: Direct labor, direct materials, subcontractor costs
Costs that allocate to contract (allocation of depreciation, insurance)
not_capitalizable: General and administrative costs (unless explicitly chargeable)
Wasted materials, labor, or other resources
Costs related to satisfied or partially satisfied performance obligations
Costs for which entity cannot determine whether they relate to unsatisfied or satisfied POs

amortization.method: Systematic basis consistent with transfer of goods/services to which asset relates
amortization.typical_approach: Same pattern as revenue recognition for related PO
amortization.update_amortization: If expected contract period changes, adjust amortization prospectively

impairment.when_to_test: At least annually or when indicator exists
impairment.impairment_test: Compare carrying amount to remaining consideration expected less costs directly related to providing goods/services not yet recognized as expenses
impairment.impairment_loss: Recognize to extent carrying amount exceeds recoverable amount
impairment.reversal: If conditions improve, reverse impairment (up to original carrying amount)

assurance_type_warranty.description: Warranty that assures customer the product complies with agreed-upon specifications
assurance_type_warranty.accounting: NOT a separate performance obligation; accrue under ASC 450 (contingencies)
indicators: Warranty provides protection against defects that existed at sale date

service_type_warranty.description: Warranty that provides a service beyond assuring product compliance
service_type_warranty.accounting: Separate performance obligation; allocate portion of transaction price
indicators: Customer has option to purchase warranty separately
Warranty provides coverage for issues arising after sale
Warranty provides services beyond defect protection (e.g., maintenance)

combination_warranty.scenario: Warranty has both assurance and service components
combination_warranty.accounting: Allocate transaction price to service component if separately identifiable; remainder follows assurance accounting

functional_intellectual_property.description: IP has significant standalone functionality (e.g., software, biological compound)
functional_intellectual_property.revenue_recognition: Point in time (when customer obtains license)
characteristics: Functionality is not expected to substantially change
Customer can derive substantial benefit from IP in its current form

symbolic_intellectual_property.description: IP doesn't have significant standalone functionality (e.g., brand, trademark, logo)
characteristics: Value is substantially derived from entity's ongoing or past activities
Customer depends on entity's continuing activities
examples: Brand licensing where licensor continues marketing to maintain brand value
Franchise rights where franchisor provides ongoing support

sales_based_or_usage_based_royalties.exception: Special exception for licenses of IP
sales_based_or_usage_based_royalties.recognition: Recognize revenue when later of: (a) subsequent sale or usage occurs, or (b) performance obligation to which royalty is allocated is satisfied (or partially satisfied)
sales_based_or_usage_based_royalties.rationale: Exception prevents recognizing revenue before customer's sales/usage occurs
sales_based_or_usage_based_royalties.example: Software license with 5% royalty on customer's sales. Recognize royalty revenue as customer makes sales, even if license granted earlier.

principal_vs_agent.determination: Is entity a principal (controls good/service before transfer to customer) or agent (arranges for another party to provide good/service)?
principal_indicators: Entity is primarily responsible for fulfilling promise
Entity has inventory risk before or after transfer to customer
Entity has discretion in establishing prices
agent_indicators: Another party is primarily responsible for fulfillment
Entity earns commission or fee for arranging transaction
Entity does not have inventory risk

revenue_recognition.revenue: Gross amount of consideration (full sales price)
revenue_recognition.cost: Amount paid to other party is cost of goods sold
No COGS; only net fee is revenue

example.scenario: Online retailer lists third-party products. Customer pays $100. Retailer keeps $15, pays $85 to supplier.
example.analysis_factors: Who sets price? Who has inventory risk? Who is responsible for fulfillment and returns?

forward_or_call_option.description: Entity has obligation or right to repurchase asset
accounting: If repurchase price ≥ original selling price: Lease (ASC 842) or financing arrangement
If repurchase price < original selling price and > expected market value: Lease
If repurchase price < original selling price and ≤ expected market value: Sale with right of return

put_option.description: Customer has right to require entity to repurchase asset
accounting: If customer has significant economic incentive to exercise: Lease or financing
If repurchase price < original selling price: Sale with right of return

indicators: Product controlled by entity until specified event (e.g., sale to end customer)
Entity can require return or transfer to another party
Dealer doesn't have unconditional obligation to pay
consignment_arrangements.accounting: Do NOT recognize revenue when transferring to dealer; recognize when dealer sells to end customer or specified event occurs

gift_cards_and_breakage.initial_accounting: Record liability when gift card sold

breakage.definition: Rights expected not to be redeemed
breakage.recognition: Recognize breakage revenue in proportion to pattern of rights exercised if entity expects to be entitled to breakage
breakage.conditions: Remote that legal obligation to remit to government will arise
breakage.example: Sell $100K in gift cards, expect 10% breakage ($10K). As cards redeemed, recognize proportionate breakage. If $45K redeemed (50% of expected $90K redemptions), recognize $45K revenue + $5K breakage (50% of $10K expected breakage) = $50K total revenue.

disclosures: Revenue recognized from contracts with customers separately from other sources
Impairment losses on receivables or contract assets
Information about performance obligations (when satisfied, significant payment terms, nature of goods/services, obligations for returns/refunds/warranties)
Information about significant judgments (methods/inputs/assumptions for determining transaction price, allocating to POs, measuring progress)
Opening and closing balances of receivables, contract assets, contract liabilities
Revenue recognized in period from amounts included in opening contract liability
Revenue recognized from performance obligations satisfied in previous periods
Explanation of significant changes in contract asset and liability balances
Aggregate amount of transaction price allocated to unsatisfied (or partially unsatisfied) POs
When entity expects to recognize that amount as revenue
Practical expedient available for contracts ≤ 1 year

qualitative_and_quantitative.category: Costs to obtain or fulfill contracts
disclosures: Judgments made in determining amount of costs incurred to obtain or fulfill contracts
Method used to amortize capitalized costs
Amount of amortization and impairment losses

disaggregation_of_revenue.requirement: Disaggregate revenue into categories that depict how nature, amount, timing, and uncertainty of revenue and cash flows are affected by economic factors
examples_of_categories: Timing of transfer (point in time vs. over time)
disaggregation_of_revenue.objective: Enable users to understand relationship between disaggregated revenue and revenue information by reportable segment

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Confusing performance obligation identification with deliverables
common_pitfalls.tip: Remember: distinct within context matters, not just capable of being distinct

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Forgetting to apply constraint on variable consideration
common_pitfalls.tip: Even if you estimate variable consideration, ask: is it probable there won't be significant reversal?

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Allocating transaction price evenly instead of using SSP
common_pitfalls.tip: Always allocate based on relative standalone selling prices, not evenly

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Recognizing revenue over time when criteria not met
common_pitfalls.tip: All three criteria must be tested; most contracts don't meet criteria

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Using wrong progress measure for over-time recognition
common_pitfalls.tip: Cost-to-cost is input method; must exclude uninstalled materials and other non-contributing costs

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Treating all warranties as separate performance obligations
common_pitfalls.tip: Only service-type warranties are POs; assurance warranties are accrued under ASC 450
Focus on control: does entity control good/service before transfer to customer?

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Recognizing revenue on consignment when transferring to dealer
common_pitfalls.tip: Consignment = recognize when dealer sells to end customer, not when shipped to dealer

multiple_choice_tips: Read stem carefully for key words: 'distinct,' 'probable,' 'control,' 'over time'
Identify which step of five-step model is being tested
For performance obligations: check both criteria (capable AND distinct in context)
For variable consideration: estimate it, then apply constraint
For timing: test all three over-time criteria before defaulting to point in time
For principal vs. agent: ask who controls good/service before transfer to customer
Watch for 'EXCEPT' questions - they often test knowledge of exceptions to general rules
simulation_tips: Show your work step-by-step through five-step model
For journal entries: ensure debits equal credits; use proper account titles
For performance obligation identification: explicitly state why item is/isn't distinct

practice_problems.topic: Performance obligation identification and transaction price allocation
practice_problems.question:
TechCorp enters into a contract with a customer to provide the following:

- Custom server equipment: TechCorp's standalone selling price is $500,000
- Installation services: TechCorp's standalone selling price is $100,000
- 3-year maintenance contract: TechCorp's standalone selling price is $150,000

The total contract price is $650,000. The installation is highly specialized and customizes the equipment to work with the customer's existing infrastructure.

Required:
(a) Identify the performance obligations in this contract.
(b) Allocate the transaction price to each performance obligation.
(c) If the equipment and installation are completed in Year 1 and the maintenance is provided evenly over Years 2-4, how much revenue should TechCorp recognize in Year 1?

part_a.analysis:
Apply the two distinct criteria:

1. Equipment + Installation:
   - Capable of being distinct? Equipment alone could be used, but installation is highly specialized
   - Distinct within context? NO - installation significantly customizes the equipment
   - Conclusion: Equipment and installation are ONE performance obligation (integrated solution)

2. Maintenance:
   - Capable of being distinct? YES - customer could obtain maintenance elsewhere
   - Distinct within context? YES - maintenance is separate service not integrated with equipment
   - Conclusion: Maintenance is a SEPARATE performance obligation

Performance Obligations:
- PO #1: Equipment with installation (combined)
- PO #2: 3-year maintenance
part_a.answer: Two performance obligations: (1) Equipment with installation, (2) Maintenance

calculation: Note: Equipment and installation are one PO, so combine their SSPs:
- PO #2 satisfied ratably over 3 years: $130,000 / 3 = $43,333 per year

key_learning_points: Installation that significantly customizes equipment makes the items NOT distinct within context
Combine SSPs for performance obligations that include multiple promised goods/services
Maintenance contracts typically represent separate performance obligations satisfied over time
Contract liability is used when cash received exceeds revenue recognized

practice_problems.topic: Variable consideration, constraint, and over-time recognition
practice_problems.question:
BuildRight Construction enters into a contract on January 1, Year 1 to construct a commercial building. Contract details:

- Base contract price: $20,000,000
- Performance bonus: $2,000,000 if building completed by December 31, Year 2 (on time)
- Performance penalty: $500,000 if building NOT completed by December 31, Year 2
- BuildRight estimates 70% probability of on-time completion based on experience with similar projects
- Total estimated costs: $16,000,000
- Year 1 actual costs incurred: $6,400,000
- Year 2 estimated costs to complete: $10,400,000 (revised from original estimate)

The contract meets the criteria for over-time revenue recognition. BuildRight uses the cost-to-cost method to measure progress.

Required:
(a) Determine the transaction price at contract inception.
(b) Calculate revenue to recognize in Year 1.
(c) If Year 2 actual costs are $10,400,000 and the building is completed on time, calculate the cumulative catch-up adjustment in Year 2.

step_1_estimate_variable_consideration.description: Determine most likely amount or expected value
most_likely_amount_method: Most likely outcome: On-time completion (70% probability)
step_1_estimate_variable_consideration.choice: Use most likely amount method (only two possible outcomes, one clearly more likely)

step_2_apply_constraint.question: Is it probable that a significant reversal will NOT occur?
factors_to_consider: Amount is susceptible to factors outside entity's influence (✓ some risk - weather, labor, permits)
Uncertainty expected to be resolved in reasonable time (✓ 2 years)
Entity has experience with similar contracts (✓ has experience)
Entity has practice of offering concessions (✗ not mentioned)
Large range of possible amounts (✗ only two scenarios: +$2M or -$500K)
step_2_apply_constraint.conclusion: 70% probability meets 'probable' threshold (>50-75%). Entity has experience with similar projects. Risk of reversal exists but not highly susceptible to uncontrollable factors.
step_2_apply_constraint.decision: Include the $2,000,000 bonus in transaction price (constrain penalty portion for conservatism)
step_2_apply_constraint.alternative_conservative_approach: Some may argue to use $20,000,000 base only if reversal risk is deemed too high

part_a.answer: Transaction price: $22,000,000 (base $20M + bonus $2M, based on most likely amount method and constraint assessment)

revised_estimates: Building completed ON TIME, so bonus earned: $22,000,000 (confirmed)
alternative_calculation_showing_cost_ove: If we calculate what Year 1 revenue WOULD have been with revised cost estimate:
part_c.note: The cumulative catch-up adjustment reflects both the additional progress in Year 2 (from 40% to 100%) and the correction for the cost overrun impact on Year 1's percentage. Total project revenue of $22,000,000 is achieved.

Constraint requires assessment of whether significant reversal is probable
Most likely amount method is appropriate when there are two outcomes and one is clearly more probable
Cost-to-cost method requires updating estimates each period and recognizing cumulative catch-up adjustments
When costs exceed original estimates, percentage complete in prior periods decreases retrospectively

practice_problems.topic: Multiple performance obligations, licensing, and principal vs. agent
practice_problems.question:
SoftServe Inc. enters into the following arrangement with Client Co. on July 1, Year 1:

1. Perpetual license to SoftServe's existing data analytics software: SoftServe's standalone selling price is $600,000. The software has significant standalone functionality and does not require SoftServe's ongoing activities to maintain its value.

2. Customization services to integrate the software with Client's systems: SoftServe's standalone selling price is $200,000.

3. SoftServe will arrange for DataHost Inc. to provide cloud hosting for Client. DataHost will charge Client $50,000 per year, but Client pays SoftServe $65,000 per year, and SoftServe pays DataHost. SoftServe does not control the hosting services before they are transferred to Client. The hosting arrangement is for 2 years.

Total amount Client pays to SoftServe: $900,000 for license and customization (paid upon delivery), plus $65,000 per year for hosting.

Required:
(a) Identify the performance obligations.
(b) Determine whether SoftServe is principal or agent for the hosting services.
(c) Allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations.
(d) Determine when revenue should be recognized for each performance obligation.
(e) Calculate total revenue SoftServe will recognize over the 2-year hosting period.

analysis: - Capable of being distinct? YES - has standalone functionality
- Distinct in context? YES - not significantly integrated with customization
- Capable of being distinct? Possibly - integration services can be obtained elsewhere
- Distinct in context? YES - doesn't significantly modify the software license itself
- This is provided by DataHost, need to assess principal vs. agent
- If agent: commission is part of transaction price but not separate PO
- If principal: hosting is separate performance obligation
part_a.answer: Two performance obligations: (1) Software license, (2) Customization services. Hosting is evaluated separately for principal vs. agent.

indicators.assessment: SoftServe has no inventory risk for hosting - AGENT indicator
SoftServe sets price to Client ($65K vs. $50K cost) - could indicate PRINCIPAL
SoftServe does NOT control hosting before transfer - AGENT indicator (this is determinative)

principal_vs_agent_analysis.conclusion: SoftServe is an AGENT for hosting services

part_b.answer: Agent - SoftServe does not control hosting services before they are transferred to Client

transaction_price_determination: Hosting commission: ($65,000 - $50,000) × 2 years = $30,000 (this is SoftServe's commission as agent)
Note: As agent, SoftServe recognizes only the NET amount ($15K/year commission), NOT the gross $65K
allocation: For the $900,000 only (hosting commission is recognized as earned):
part_c.answer: License: $675,000 | Customization: $225,000 | Hosting commission: $15,000 per year (recognized as services are provided)

license.timing: Point in time (when license is transferred to Client)
license.reasoning: Functional IP with standalone functionality = point-in-time recognition
license.date: When software is delivered and Client can begin using it

customization.timing: Point in time or over time depending on facts
customization.reasoning: If customization meets over-time criteria (e.g., enhances asset Client controls), recognize over time. Otherwise, at completion.
customization.assumption: Assume point in time at completion for this problem

hosting_commission.timing: Over time as hosting services are provided (ratably over 2 years)
hosting_commission.reasoning: Agent recognizes commission as the services are arranged and provided

part_d.answer: License: Point in time upon delivery | Customization: Point in time upon completion | Hosting commission: Over 2 years ratably

python_examples.title: Revenue Recognition Calculator - Five-Step Model
python_examples.description: A comprehensive calculator that implements the five-step revenue recognition model, including transaction price allocation, variable consideration, and over-time recognition using cost-to-cost method.
python_examples.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Revenue Recognition Calculator - ASC 606 Five-Step Model

This module provides classes and functions to calculate revenue recognition
under ASC 606, including:
- Performance obligation identification
- Transaction price determination (including variable consideration)
- Allocation using standalone selling prices
- Over-time and point-in-time recognition
- Cost-to-cost progress measurement
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Optional, Tuple
from enum import Enum
import json


class RecognitionTiming(Enum):
    """Revenue recognition timing types"""
    POINT_IN_TIME = "point_in_time"
    OVER_TIME = "over_time"


class VariableConsiderationMethod(Enum):
    """Methods for estimating variable consideration"""
    EXPECTED_VALUE = "expected_value"
    MOST_LIKELY_AMOUNT = "most_likely_amount"


@dataclass
class PerformanceObligation:
    """Represents a performance obligation in a contract"""
    id: str
    description: str
    standalone_selling_price: float
    allocated_price: float = 0.0
    recognition_timing: RecognitionTiming = RecognitionTiming.POINT_IN_TIME
    is_satisfied: bool = False
    
    # For over-time recognition
    total_estimated_costs: Optional[float] = None
    costs_incurred_to_date: Optional[float] = None
    
    def calculate_progress_percentage(self) -> float:
        """
        Calculate percentage complete using cost-to-cost method.
        Returns value between 0.0 and 1.0.
        """
        if self.recognition_timing != RecognitionTiming.OVER_TIME:
            return 1.0 if self.is_satisfied else 0.0
        
        if not self.total_estimated_costs or self.total_estimated_costs == 0:
            return 0.0
        
        costs = self.costs_incurred_to_date or 0.0
        return min(costs / self.total_estimated_costs, 1.0)
    
    def calculate_revenue_to_recognize(self) -> float:
        """
        Calculate revenue to recognize based on progress.
        """
        if self.recognition_timing == RecognitionTiming.POINT_IN_TIME:
            return self.allocated_price if self.is_satisfied else 0.0
        
        # Over time recognition
        progress = self.calculate_progress_percentage()
        return self.allocated_price * progress


@dataclass
class VariableConsiderationScenario:
    """Represents a scenario for variable consideration calculation"""
    description: str
    amount: float
    probability: float


class VariableConsideration:
    """Handles variable consideration estimation and constraint"""
    
    def __init__(self, scenarios: List[VariableConsiderationScenario]):
        self.scenarios = scenarios
    
    def calculate_expected_value(self) -> float:
        """
        Calculate expected value (probability-weighted average).
        """
        return sum(s.amount * s.probability for s in self.scenarios)
    
    def calculate_most_likely_amount(self) -> float:
        """
        Calculate most likely amount (scenario with highest probability).
        """
        if not self.scenarios:
            return 0.0
        return max(self.scenarios, key=lambda s: s.probability).amount
    
    def estimate(self, method: VariableConsiderationMethod) -> float:
        """
        Estimate variable consideration using specified method.
        """
        if method == VariableConsiderationMethod.EXPECTED_VALUE:
            return self.calculate_expected_value()
        else:
            return self.calculate_most_likely_amount()
    
    def apply_constraint(self, estimated_amount: float, 
                        reversal_probability_threshold: float = 0.25) -> float:
        """
        Apply constraint on variable consideration.
        
        Include variable consideration only if probability of significant
        reversal is below threshold (default 25%, meaning 75% probable
        that reversal will NOT occur).
        
        This is simplified; in practice, requires detailed analysis.
        """
        # Calculate probability of scenarios below estimated amount
        # (proxy for reversal risk)
        reversal_prob = sum(
            s.probability for s in self.scenarios 
            if s.amount < estimated_amount * 0.8  # Significant = 20% difference
        )
        
        if reversal_prob <= reversal_probability_threshold:
            return estimated_amount
        else:
            # Conservative: use lowest scenario amount
            return min(s.amount for s in self.scenarios)


class Contract:
    """Represents a customer contract under ASC 606"""
    
    def __init__(self, contract_id: str, customer_name: str):
        self.contract_id = contract_id
        self.customer_name = customer_name
        self.performance_obligations: List[PerformanceObligation] = []
        self.fixed_consideration = 0.0
        self.variable_consideration: Optional[VariableConsideration] = None
        self.variable_consideration_method = VariableConsiderationMethod.MOST_LIKELY_AMOUNT
        self.total_transaction_price = 0.0
    
    def add_performance_obligation(self, po: PerformanceObligation):
        """Add a performance obligation to the contract"""
        self.performance_obligations.append(po)
    
    def set_variable_consideration(self, 
                                  scenarios: List[VariableConsiderationScenario],
                                  method: VariableConsiderationMethod):
        """Set variable consideration scenarios and estimation method"""
        self.variable_consideration = VariableConsideration(scenarios)
        self.variable_consideration_method = method
    
    def determine_transaction_price(self) -> float:
        """
        Step 3: Determine the transaction price.
        """
        total = self.fixed_consideration
        
        if self.variable_consideration:
            estimated = self.variable_consideration.estimate(
                self.variable_consideration_method
            )
            constrained = self.variable_consideration.apply_constraint(estimated)
            total += constrained
        
        self.total_transaction_price = total
        return total
    
    def allocate_transaction_price(self):
        """
        Step 4: Allocate transaction price to performance obligations
        based on relative standalone selling prices.
        """
        if not self.performance_obligations:
            return
        
        # Calculate total SSP
        total_ssp = sum(po.standalone_selling_price 
                       for po in self.performance_obligations)
        
        if total_ssp == 0:
            return
        
        # Allocate proportionately
        for po in self.performance_obligations:
            allocation_percentage = po.standalone_selling_price / total_ssp
            po.allocated_price = self.total_transaction_price * allocation_percentage
    
    def calculate_total_revenue_recognized(self) -> float:
        """
        Step 5: Calculate total revenue recognized across all
        performance obligations based on current progress.
        """
        return sum(po.calculate_revenue_to_recognize() 
                  for po in self.performance_obligations)
    
    def get_revenue_by_performance_obligation(self) -> List[Tuple[str, float]]:
        """
        Get revenue recognized for each performance obligation.
        """
        return [
            (po.description, po.calculate_revenue_to_recognize())
            for po in self.performance_obligations
        ]
    
    def generate_report(self) -> dict:
        """
        Generate comprehensive revenue recognition report.
        """
        return {
            "contract_id": self.contract_id,
            "customer": self.customer_name,
            "transaction_price": {
                "fixed_consideration": self.fixed_consideration,
                "variable_consideration": {
                    "estimated": self.variable_consideration.estimate(
                        self.variable_consideration_method
                    ) if self.variable_consideration else 0.0,
                    "method": self.variable_consideration_method.value 
                             if self.variable_consideration else None
                },
                "total": self.total_transaction_price
            },
            "performance_obligations": [
                {
                    "id": po.id,
                    "description": po.description,
                    "standalone_selling_price": po.standalone_selling_price,
                    "allocated_price": po.allocated_price,
                    "recognition_timing": po.recognition_timing.value,
                    "progress_percentage": po.calculate_progress_percentage() * 100,
                    "revenue_recognized": po.calculate_revenue_to_recognize(),
                    "is_satisfied": po.is_satisfied
                }
                for po in self.performance_obligations
            ],
            "total_revenue_recognized": self.calculate_total_revenue_recognized()
        }


# Example Usage
def example_construction_contract():
    """
    Example: Construction contract with variable consideration
    (similar to Practice Problem #2)
    """
    print("=" * 70)
    print("CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT REVENUE RECOGNITION EXAMPLE")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    # Create contract
    contract = Contract("CONST-2025-001", "BuildRight Construction")
    
    # Set consideration
    contract.fixed_consideration = 20_000_000
    
    # Variable consideration scenarios
    scenarios = [
        VariableConsiderationScenario(
            description="On-time completion with bonus",
            amount=22_000_000,  # $20M base + $2M bonus
            probability=0.70
        ),
        VariableConsiderationScenario(
            description="Late completion with penalty",
            amount=19_500_000,  # $20M base - $500K penalty
            probability=0.30
        )
    ]
    
    contract.set_variable_consideration(
        scenarios, 
        VariableConsiderationMethod.MOST_LIKELY_AMOUNT
    )
    
    # Determine transaction price
    transaction_price = contract.determine_transaction_price()
    print(f"\nTransaction Price: ${transaction_price:,.2f}")
    
    # Add performance obligation (construction is one PO)
    po = PerformanceObligation(
        id="PO-001",
        description="Construction of commercial building",
        standalone_selling_price=22_000_000,  # Use expected price as SSP
        recognition_timing=RecognitionTiming.OVER_TIME,
        total_estimated_costs=16_000_000,
        costs_incurred_to_date=6_400_000  # Year 1 costs
    )
    
    contract.add_performance_obligation(po)
    
    # Allocate (only one PO, gets full amount)
    contract.allocate_transaction_price()
    
    # Calculate revenue
    print(f"\nYear 1 Progress: {po.calculate_progress_percentage() * 100:.1f}%")
    print(f"Year 1 Revenue Recognized: ${po.calculate_revenue_to_recognize():,.2f}")
    
    # Generate full report
    report = contract.generate_report()
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("REVENUE RECOGNITION REPORT")
    print("=" * 70)
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))


def example_multiple_performance_obligations():
    """
    Example: Contract with multiple performance obligations
    (similar to Practice Problem #1)
    """
    print("\n\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("MULTIPLE PERFORMANCE OBLIGATIONS EXAMPLE")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    # Create contract
    contract = Contract("TECH-2025-001", "TechCorp")
    contract.fixed_consideration = 650_000
    
    # Determine transaction price (no variable consideration)
    contract.determine_transaction_price()
    
    # Add performance obligations
    po1 = PerformanceObligation(
        id="PO-001",
        description="Equipment with Installation",
        standalone_selling_price=600_000,  # Combined SSP
        recognition_timing=RecognitionTiming.POINT_IN_TIME,
        is_satisfied=True  # Completed in Year 1
    )
    
    po2 = PerformanceObligation(
        id="PO-002",
        description="3-Year Maintenance Contract",
        standalone_selling_price=150_000,
        recognition_timing=RecognitionTiming.OVER_TIME,
        total_estimated_costs=90_000,
        costs_incurred_to_date=0  # Year 1, no maintenance yet
    )
    
    contract.add_performance_obligation(po1)
    contract.add_performance_obligation(po2)
    
    # Allocate transaction price
    contract.allocate_transaction_price()
    
    print(f"\nTransaction Price: ${contract.total_transaction_price:,.2f}")
    print(f"\nPO #1 Allocation: ${po1.allocated_price:,.2f}")
    print(f"PO #2 Allocation: ${po2.allocated_price:,.2f}")
    
    # Calculate revenue
    revenue_by_po = contract.get_revenue_by_performance_obligation()
    print("\nYear 1 Revenue by Performance Obligation:")
    for desc, revenue in revenue_by_po:
        print(f"  {desc}: ${revenue:,.2f}")
    
    print(f"\nTotal Year 1 Revenue: ${contract.calculate_total_revenue_recognized():,.2f}")
    
    # Generate report
    report = contract.generate_report()
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("REVENUE RECOGNITION REPORT")
    print("=" * 70)
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Run examples
    example_construction_contract()
    example_multiple_performance_obligations()
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("Examples completed successfully!")
    print("=" * 70)

python_examples.title: Contract Modification Analyzer
python_examples.description: Tool to determine the appropriate accounting treatment for contract modifications under ASC 606.
python_examples.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Contract Modification Analyzer - ASC 606

Determines the appropriate accounting treatment for contract modifications:
- Separate contract
- Prospective adjustment
- Cumulative catch-up adjustment
- Combination approach
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum
from typing import List, Optional


class ModificationTreatment(Enum):
    """Types of contract modification accounting treatments"""
    SEPARATE_CONTRACT = "separate_contract"
    PROSPECTIVE = "prospective"
    CUMULATIVE_CATCHUP = "cumulative_catchup"
    COMBINATION = "combination"


@dataclass
class OriginalContract:
    """Original contract terms"""
    contract_id: str
    original_price: float
    goods_services_delivered: float  # Value already delivered
    goods_services_remaining: float  # Value remaining to deliver
    revenue_recognized_to_date: float
    are_remaining_goods_distinct: bool


@dataclass
class Modification:
    """Contract modification details"""
    modification_id: str
    added_goods_services: float  # Value of goods/services added
    price_for_added_items: float  # Price charged for added items
    are_added_goods_distinct: bool
    is_price_at_standalone_selling_price: bool


class ContractModificationAnalyzer:
    """Analyzes contract modifications and determines accounting treatment"""
    
    def __init__(self, original: OriginalContract, modification: Modification):
        self.original = original
        self.modification = modification
        self.treatment: Optional[ModificationTreatment] = None
        self.analysis_steps: List[str] = []
    
    def analyze(self) -> ModificationTreatment:
        """
        Analyze the modification and determine accounting treatment.
        """
        self.analysis_steps = []
        
        # Step 1: Check if modification adds distinct goods at SSP
        self.analysis_steps.append(
            "Step 1: Does modification add distinct goods/services at standalone selling price?"
        )
        
        if (self.modification.are_added_goods_distinct and 
            self.modification.is_price_at_standalone_selling_price):
            
            self.analysis_steps.append(
                "  ✓ YES - Added items are distinct AND priced at SSP"
            )
            self.analysis_steps.append(
                "  CONCLUSION: Account for as SEPARATE CONTRACT"
            )
            self.treatment = ModificationTreatment.SEPARATE_CONTRACT
            return self.treatment
        
        self.analysis_steps.append(
            "  ✗ NO - Either added items not distinct OR not priced at SSP"
        )
        
        # Step 2: Check if remaining goods/services are distinct
        self.analysis_steps.append(
            "\nStep 2: Are remaining goods/services distinct from those already transferred?"
        )
        
        if self.original.are_remaining_goods_distinct:
            self.analysis_steps.append(
                "  ✓ YES - Remaining goods/services are distinct"
            )
            self.analysis_steps.append(
                "  CONCLUSION: Account for using PROSPECTIVE method"
            )
            self.analysis_steps.append(
                "  Terminate old contract, create new contract for remaining obligations"
            )
            self.treatment = ModificationTreatment.PROSPECTIVE
            return self.treatment
        
        self.analysis_steps.append(
            "  ✗ NO - Remaining goods/services are NOT distinct"
        )
        
        # Step 3: Remaining goods not distinct - use cumulative catch-up
        self.analysis_steps.append(
            "\nStep 3: Since remaining goods/services are not distinct:"
        )
        self.analysis_steps.append(
            "  CONCLUSION: Account for using CUMULATIVE CATCH-UP method"
        )
        self.analysis_steps.append(
            "  Adjust revenue as if modification was part of original contract"
        )
        
        self.treatment = ModificationTreatment.CUMULATIVE_CATCHUP
        return self.treatment
    
    def calculate_revenue_adjustment(self) -> dict:
        """
        Calculate the revenue adjustment based on the treatment.
        """
        if not self.treatment:
            self.analyze()
        
        result = {
            "treatment": self.treatment.value,
            "analysis": "\n".join(self.analysis_steps)
        }
        
        if self.treatment == ModificationTreatment.SEPARATE_CONTRACT:
            result["accounting"] = {
                "original_contract": {
                    "continue_as_before": True,
                    "no_adjustment_needed": True
                },
                "new_contract": {
                    "revenue": self.modification.price_for_added_items,
                    "description": "Account for added goods/services separately"
                }
            }
        
        elif self.treatment == ModificationTreatment.PROSPECTIVE:
            new_transaction_price = (
                self.original.original_price + 
                self.modification.price_for_added_items -
                self.original.revenue_recognized_to_date
            )
            
            result["accounting"] = {
                "terminate_old_contract": True,
                "new_contract_for_remaining_obligations": {
                    "transaction_price": new_transaction_price,
                    "includes": "Original remaining + modification additions",
                    "description": "Recognize over remaining performance period"
                },
                "no_adjustment_to_previously_recognized_revenue": True
            }
        
        elif self.treatment == ModificationTreatment.CUMULATIVE_CATCHUP:
            # Calculate as if modification was part of original contract
            modified_total_price = (
                self.original.original_price + 
                self.modification.price_for_added_items
            )
            
            # Assume percentage complete based on value delivered
            total_value = (
                self.original.goods_services_delivered + 
                self.original.goods_services_remaining +
                self.modification.added_goods_services
            )
            
            percentage_complete = (
                self.original.goods_services_delivered / total_value
                if total_value > 0 else 0
            )
            
            revenue_should_have_recognized = (
                modified_total_price * percentage_complete
            )
            
            catchup_adjustment = (
                revenue_should_have_recognized - 
                self.original.revenue_recognized_to_date
            )
            
            result["accounting"] = {
                "modified_total_transaction_price": modified_total_price,
                "percentage_complete": percentage_complete * 100,
                "revenue_should_have_recognized": revenue_should_have_recognized,
                "revenue_already_recognized": self.original.revenue_recognized_to_date,
                "cumulative_catchup_adjustment": catchup_adjustment,
                "description": (
                    "Recognize catch-up adjustment in current period. "
                    "Future revenue based on modified total price."
                )
            }
        
        return result
    
    def generate_report(self) -> str:
        """
        Generate a formatted report of the analysis.
        """
        result = self.calculate_revenue_adjustment()
        
        report = []
        report.append("=" * 70)
        report.append("CONTRACT MODIFICATION ANALYSIS REPORT")
        report.append("=" * 70)
        report.append(f"\nModification ID: {self.modification.modification_id}")
        report.append(f"Original Contract: {self.original.contract_id}")
        report.append("\n" + result["analysis"])
        report.append("\n" + "=" * 70)
        report.append("ACCOUNTING TREATMENT")
        report.append("=" * 70)
        
        import json
        report.append(json.dumps(result["accounting"], indent=2))
        
        return "\n".join(report)


# Example Usage
def example_separate_contract():
    """
    Example: Modification that qualifies as separate contract
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("EXAMPLE 1: SEPARATE CONTRACT")
    print("=" * 70)
    print("\nScenario: Software company adds 100 additional user licenses")
    print("at standard $50/user price to existing 500-user contract.")
    
    original = OriginalContract(
        contract_id="SW-2024-001",
        original_price=500_000,  # 500 users × $1000/user
        goods_services_delivered=250_000,  # 50% complete
        goods_services_remaining=250_000,
        revenue_recognized_to_date=250_000,
        are_remaining_goods_distinct=True
    )
    
    modification = Modification(
        modification_id="MOD-001",
        added_goods_services=100_000,  # 100 additional users
        price_for_added_items=100_000,  # 100 × $1000 (same SSP)
        are_added_goods_distinct=True,
        is_price_at_standalone_selling_price=True
    )
    
    analyzer = ContractModificationAnalyzer(original, modification)
    print(analyzer.generate_report())


def example_prospective():
    """
    Example: Modification requiring prospective treatment
    """
    print("\n\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("EXAMPLE 2: PROSPECTIVE TREATMENT")
    print("=" * 70)
    print("\nScenario: Consulting contract adds additional distinct services")
    print("but at discounted price (not SSP).")
    
    original = OriginalContract(
        contract_id="CONS-2024-001",
        original_price=300_000,
        goods_services_delivered=100_000,  # 1/3 complete
        goods_services_remaining=200_000,
        revenue_recognized_to_date=100_000,
        are_remaining_goods_distinct=True
    )
    
    modification = Modification(
        modification_id="MOD-002",
        added_goods_services=150_000,
        price_for_added_items=120_000,  # Discounted from SSP of $150K
        are_added_goods_distinct=True,
        is_price_at_standalone_selling_price=False  # Discounted!
    )
    
    analyzer = ContractModificationAnalyzer(original, modification)
    print(analyzer.generate_report())


def example_cumulative_catchup():
    """
    Example: Modification requiring cumulative catch-up
    """
    print("\n\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("EXAMPLE 3: CUMULATIVE CATCH-UP TREATMENT")
    print("=" * 70)
    print("\nScenario: Construction contract adds square footage to building")
    print("(not distinct from original building construction).")
    
    original = OriginalContract(
        contract_id="BUILD-2024-001",
        original_price=10_000_000,
        goods_services_delivered=4_000_000,  # 40% complete
        goods_services_remaining=6_000_000,
        revenue_recognized_to_date=4_000_000,
        are_remaining_goods_distinct=False  # Building expansion not distinct
    )
    
    modification = Modification(
        modification_id="MOD-003",
        added_goods_services=2_000_000,  # Additional building space
        price_for_added_items=1_800_000,
        are_added_goods_distinct=False,  # Part of same building
        is_price_at_standalone_selling_price=False
    )
    
    analyzer = ContractModificationAnalyzer(original, modification)
    print(analyzer.generate_report())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    example_separate_contract()
    example_prospective()
    example_cumulative_catchup()
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("Contract modification analysis examples completed!")
    print("=" * 70)

key_takeaways: ASC 606 provides a comprehensive five-step model for revenue recognition applicable across all industries
Performance obligations must be both capable of being distinct AND distinct within the context of the contract
Variable consideration must be estimated and constrained to prevent revenue reversal
Transaction price allocation uses relative standalone selling prices
Revenue is recognized over time only if specific criteria are met; otherwise at point in time
Contract modifications require careful analysis to determine proper accounting treatment
Principal vs. agent determination focuses on control before transfer to customer
Significant judgment is required at multiple steps in the model
cpa_exam_focus_areas: Five-step model application to various scenarios
Special topics: warranties, licensing, principal vs. agent, consignment
study_recommendations: Practice working through the five-step model systematically
Memorize the criteria for each step (especially distinct criteria and over-time criteria)
Work numerous practice problems involving calculations
Understand the logic behind each step, not just the mechanics
Focus on special topics that commonly appear on exam (warranties, licensing, etc.)
Practice time management with task-based simulations
